issues.description: setuptools<82 cap leaks into core runtime install_requires instead of staying a CI workaround
issues.detail: The mmcv/pkg_resources problem is a build-time CI issue. Pinning setuptools<82 in core/setup.py forces every downstream user of autogluon.core to accept a capped setuptools forever. That's the wrong scope. Cap it in the CI scripts where the FIXME already lives; don't push the workaround onto users.

issues.description: mmcv installed with --no-build-isolation without ensuring required build deps are present
issues.detail: Disabling build isolation means the active env must already have torch, ninja, and a compatible setuptools/wheel before mmcv builds. The script installs setuptools<82 but assumes torch is preinstalled by the caller. If that ordering ever drifts the build silently breaks with a confusing error. State the precondition or install the deps explicitly.

issues.description: mmdet bumped from 3.2.0 to 3.3.0 with no justification in the commit
issues.detail: The PR is titled "Fix mmengine failure" but quietly bumps mmdet a minor version. That's a second change riding a bug fix. THREE-PATCHES territory. If 3.3.0 is required for compatibility with mmengine 0.10.7 / mmcv 2.1.0, say so in the diff comment. Otherwise split it.

issues.description: FIXME comments point to the issue but give no revert criteria or owner
issues.detail: Two FIXMEs reference mmcv#3325. Fine. Neither says what condition flips the cap off ("once mmcv releases a wheel that doesn't import pkg_resources at build time") nor who owns checking. Six months from now someone greps FIXME, finds this, and has to reverse-engineer the trigger. Add the actual revert condition.

issues.description: mim install replaced by raw pip install loses dependency resolution mim was doing
issues.detail: mim install mmcv pulls a prebuilt wheel matched to the installed torch/CUDA. Switching to plain pip with --no-build-isolation forces a source build and drops that matching logic. Likely fine in CI where torch is pinned, but worth a one-line comment so the next person doesn't "clean up" back to mim and break it.

review.summary: NEEDS-WORK. The CI fix itself is reasonable: pin setuptools<82 to dodge the pkg_resources removal that breaks mmcv's build, install mmengine from PyPI instead of a git SHA. Good — pinning a workaround with a FIXME tied to an upstream issue is exactly how you do this. But the patch does more than one thing: it also leaks the setuptools cap into core/setup.py runtime requirements (wrong scope — this is a build problem, not a user problem) and silently bumps mmdet 3.2.0 to 3.3.0 with no rationale. Split those. The FIXMEs also don't state the revert condition, which guarantees someone wastes time on this again in six months.
